"""Tests for roman.py — to_roman, from_roman, and round-trip."""

import pytest
from roman import to_roman, from_roman


# ── to_roman ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

class TestToRoman:
    """Validate integer → Roman numeral conversion."""

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("n,expected", [
        (1, "I"),
        (2, "II"),
        (3, "III"),
        (4, "IV"),
        (5, "V"),
        (9, "IX"),
        (10, "X"),
        (40, "XL"),
        (49, "XLIX"),
        (50, "L"),
        (90, "XC"),
        (99, "XCIX"),
        (400, "CD"),
        (499, "CDXCIX"),
        (500, "D"),
        (900, "CM"),
        (999, "CMXCIX"),
        (1000, "M"),
        (1999, "MCMXCIX"),
        (2000, "MM"),
        (2024, "MMXXIV"),
        (3000, "MMM"),
        (3999, "MMMCMXCIX"),
    ])
    def test_known_values(self, n, expected):
        assert to_roman(n) == expected

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("n", [-1, 0, 4000, 10000, -999])
    def test_out_of_range(self, n):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            to_roman(n)

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("n", [1.0, 1.5, "1", True, False, None, 3.14])
    def test_non_integer(self, n):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            to_roman(n)


# ── from_roman ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

class TestFromRoman:
    """Validate Roman numeral → integer conversion."""

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("s,expected", [
        ("I", 1),
        ("II", 2),
        ("III", 3),
        ("IV", 4),
        ("V", 5),
        ("IX", 9),
        ("X", 10),
        ("XL", 40),
        ("XLIX", 49),
        ("L", 50),
        ("XC", 90),
        ("XCIX", 99),
        ("CD", 400),
        ("CDXCIX", 499),
        ("D", 500),
        ("CM", 900),
        ("CMXCIX", 999),
        ("M", 1000),
        ("MCMXCIX", 1999),
        ("MM", 2000),
        ("MMXXIV", 2024),
        ("MMM", 3000),
        ("MMMCMXCIX", 3999),
    ])
    def test_known_values(self, s, expected):
        assert from_roman(s) == expected

    invalid_strings = [
        "IIII",       # four I's in a row
        "VV",         # two V's
        "IC",         # invalid subtractive pair
        "XM",         # invalid subtractive pair
        "MMMM",       # too many M's
        "",           # empty string
        "banana",     # gibberish
        "ABC",        # non-Roman chars
        "MIM",        # over-complicated / ambiguous
        "A",          # single bad char
        "LL",         # duplicate L
        "DD",         # duplicate D
        "CC",         # duplicate C is actually valid? No — CC is fine, skip
        "XCIQ",       # mixed good/bad
        " ",          # space
        "\t",         # tab
        "i",          # lowercase
        "iv",         # lowercase
        "Ix",         # mixed case
    ]

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("s", invalid_strings)
    def test_invalid_input(self, s):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            from_roman(s)

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("non_str", [None, 1, 1.5, True, False, [], {}])
    def test_non_string_input(self, non_str):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            from_roman(non_str)


# ── Round-trip ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

class TestRoundTrip:
    """from_roman(to_roman(n)) == n for every valid n."""

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("n", range(1, 4000))
    def test_round_trip(self, n):
        assert from_roman(to_roman(n)) == n
